topic.title: Clinical Prediction with Heterogeneous Health Records
topic.overview: Clinical prediction models combine measurements collected at different times, sites, and modalities to estimate patient outcomes. This topic studies representation learning, missing data sources, transfer across cohorts, and transparent domain adaptation. Its practical challenge is that the information available during retrospective training may differ substantially from what is available for a new patient.
topic.whyItMatters: Performance on a benchmark does not establish clinical benefit or reliable deployment. Missing sources, temporal irregularity, and population differences can change model behavior, while understandable explanations need evidence beyond visual appeal. These concerns motivate evaluation across realistic availability and domain conditions.
topic.evolution: A 1992 representative learns expert interpretations of myocardial images using cross-validation. Later work introduces high-resolution ICU and few-shot EHR benchmarks. CLOPPS in 2024 transfers information across sources while allowing restricted inference inputs; ExtraCare in 2026 separates invariant and domain-varying representations and relates sparse dimensions to medical concepts.
openQuestions: How can evaluation reproduce the information gaps encountered during actual clinical use?
Which explanations remain stable and useful when patient populations or recording practices change?
